Colonize, develop and conquer, taking advantage of others' choices. In the card game Race for the Galaxy, players build galactic civilizations by playing game cards in front of them that represent worlds or technical and social developments. Some worlds allow players to produce goods, which can be consumed later to gain either card draws or victory points when the appropriate technologies are available to them. These are mainly provided by the developments and worlds that are not able to produce, but the fancier production worlds also give these bonuses. [Rating: 1/10] The cards are way too busy with stupid little symbols that needs a cheat sheet that is like the Rosetta Stone to decipher! I am sure it would become easier to remember them after several plays, but I am not sure I want to invest the time or energy. Once you learn the game I would dread playing it with new players anyway, as I would have to watch them go through the same frustration of learning the damn thing. Also, there is no way in hell I would want to teach this thing to anyone for the same reasons.  I really don't see what all the fuss is over this. There is really nothing new here. San Ju

[Rating: 1/10] I am tired of having to mark cards or write on cards just to be able to play a game, to correct for game designers poor color choices and/or obliviousness to even common color-blindnesses. These issues make your game unplayable.  This is a one and will remain a one until there is a color blind accessable version.

[Rating: 1/10] Mundane graphics, OK game play. I can see why geeks like it because of the space theme.

[Rating: 1/10] It is a multiplayer solitaire. Your choices dont effect your gaming group at all or at least not very much.  Update 2016: Reduced down to 1. Since I played Roll for the Galaxy I do not see why I would under any circumstances play Race for the Galaxy which is essentially the same itch but just plays worse. Race ftG is a pain, while Roll ftG is fun!

[Rating: 1/10] I know this is a popular game for many, but it is just so overly complicated and confusing that it almost turned me off gaming forever...  I even had "an expert" teach me how to play it, and I just hated it from the get-go...

[Rating: 1/10] For some reason this, really doesn't do the trick for me although my friends are big fans.

[Rating: 1/10] Few games give me such negative visceral reaction. I don't know what it is. I hate the way it looks. I hate the way it plays. I hate the stupid little icons. Sorry so negative, but I really just can't stand this game.

[Rating: 1/10] The worst game i have ever played.{and i have been gaming for 40 years} A game with no player interaction,the player who knows the cards the best,or who draws the best cards wins.

[Rating: 1/10] Here's an idea - let's take San Juan, paste a space theme on it (including mediocre artwork) and throw away everything we've learned about card design, iconography and language to create a game that is basically impenetrable for new players. I had heard that it was bad, but I never imagined it could be THIS AWFUL. I'm sorry, I don't care if this is some kind of classic, there are so many other games that are user friendly as well as challenging and fun. Seriously PLAY SAN JUAN INSTEAD.
